<entry id="U01552">
<head-word>שְׁמַת</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (cmp. שמם) 
<italic>to be still, desolate</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—Denom. שַׁמְתָּא.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שַׁמֵּית</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (denom. of שַׁמְתָּא) 
<italic>to excommunicate, accurse</italic> M. Kat. 16
<sup>a</sup> מנלן דמְשַׁמְּתִינָן whence do we derive the authority to excommunicate (persons refusing to obey the summons of the court)? Ib.</definition>
<notes>; Shebu. 36
<sup>a</sup> שַׁמְּתֵיה וכ', v. שִׁיפוֹרָא. M. Kat. l. c. הנהו בי תלתא דמְשַׁמְּתֵי לא אתו וכ' Ms. M. (ed. דשַׁמִּיתוּ) when a court of three has declared a ban, another court of three cannot raise it. Ib. 17
<sup>a</sup> ברישא מְשַׁמֵּית וכ' first he banned himself, and then him (the guilty scholar); a. fr.—Part. pass. (h. form) מְשׁוּמָּת. Sabb. 67
<sup>a</sup> (in an incantation) ליטא תבור ומש' cursed, broken, and banned.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="U01553">
<head-word>שַׁמְתָּא</head-word>
<head-word>שַׁמְּתָא</head-word>
<head-word>שַׁמַּתָּא</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) [
<italic>desolation</italic>,] </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>curse, ban</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Gen. XLII, 37. Targ. Y. Num. XXI, 24. Targ. Cant. II, 16.—M. Kat. 17
<sup>a</sup> מאי ש' what is (the etymology of) 
<italic>shamta?</italic> Rab said שׁם̇ מ̇ית̇ה there is death; Samuel said, שְׁמָמָה יהיה (Ms. M. שַׁמָּה; Ar. שם תהא, read: שמה תהא) he shall be (be thou) a desolation. Ib. ליהוי האי גברא בש' that man (thou) be excommunicated. Ib. 16
<sup>a</sup> לא חל ש' עליה וכ' (masc.) the ban has not yet rested on him thirty days. Ib. עד דחיילא ש' וכ' (it cannot be raised) before he has been under the ban thirty days. Sot. 5
<sup>a</sup> בש' דאית ביה ובש' דלית ביה he (the scholar) in whom there is pride deserves excommunication, and also he in whom there is no pride at all. Kidd. 12
<sup>b</sup> Rab ordered to be lashed על דחלא ש' וכ' him who allowed excommunication (for contempt of court) to rest on him thirty days (and did not submit to authority). B. Mets. 70
<sup>a</sup> ולא מקבל עליה ש' דרבנ‌ן Ms. M. and does not bring upon himself the ban of the Rabbis (but obeys their summons); a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> = h. חֵרֶם, 
<italic>accursed object</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Deut. XIII, 18.—
<plural-form>Pl. שַׁמְתִּין</plural-form>. Ib. VII, 26, v. שַׁמִּיתָא.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01556">
<head-word>שֵׁן</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> c. 
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> שָׁנַן)</xref></language-reference></definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>tooth, tooth-like projection</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. VI, 5 (64
<sup>b</sup>) שן תותבת ושן של זהב an inserted (natural) tooth or an (artificial) gold tooth; (Bab. ed. שן תותכת שן וכ', Ms. O. ושן, v. Rashi a. l.). Ib. 10, v. שׁוּעָל; a. fr.—Esp. (sub. נזק) 
<italic>the damage done by an animal’s eating</italic>. B. Kam. 2
<sup>b</sup> שלשה … הקרן והשן והרגל three chief damages are mentioned (in the Scriptural text) with reference to the ox: damage by the horn, by the tooth, and by the foot. Ib. תולדה דשן, v. נְשִׁיכָה. Ib. שן יש הנאה וכ', v. הֶיזֵּק. Ib. אשן ורגל it refers to damages by the tooth and by the foot; שן ורגל היכא כתיבי where is the damage by the tooth or the foot written (in the Biblical text)? Ib. ובער זו השן 
<italic>ubhiʿer</italic> (Ex. XXII, 4) this refers to damage by the tooth; a. fr.—
<italic>Du</italic>. שִׁנַּיִים, שִׁנַּיִם, שִׁי'. Ḥull. I, 2 בכל … והש' you may cut ritually with anything, except … with teeth in the jaw. Ib. ואם החליקו שִׁינֶּיהָ and if the teeth of the saw have been made smooth. Keth. 71
<sup>b</sup> בין שיניה, v. אֶצְבַּע. Ib. 16
<sup>a</sup>, v. כֶּרֶס. Kel. XIII, 8 שניטלו שִׁינָּיו (a hackle) whose teeth are broken off. Gen. R. s. 33 חשש רבי את שיניו וכ' Rabbi suffered from tooth-ache for thirteen years. Keth. 111
<sup>b</sup> טוב המלבין ש' וכ' he who causes his neighbor to show the white of his teeth (who makes him cheerful) does better than he who gives him milk to drink. Ib. א"ת לבן ש' אלא לבון ש' read not 
<italic>l’ben shinnayim</italic> (Gen. XLIX, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> but 
<italic>libbun shinnayim</italic> (whitening of teeth, cheerfulness); a. fr.— 
<italic>any organ of the body resembling teeth, gland.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—Du.</italic> as ab. Y. Yeb. VI, beg. 7
<sup>b</sup> בית הש' that part of the vagina which has glands; מבין הש' ולפנים from the glands and farther inside; Nidd. 41
<sup>b</sup>. Ḥull. 16
<sup>b</sup> שיניו נושרות the glands of his rectum will fall off; Sabb. 82
<sup>a</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>cliff, peak</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 74 כשן הזה של וכ' (the stone which Jacob put up was) as large as the peak of Tiberias; Yalk. ib. 130; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition> (sub. של פיל) 
<italic>ivory</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 3
<sup>12</sup> (play on מי יג̇ור̇ … חזק כש̇ן̇ (ג̇ר̇ש̇ון̇ who can abide snow and hail, and cold and heat? He who is as strong as ivory (or marble?); אין שן אלא לשון חזק וכ' 
<italic>shen</italic> has the meaning 
<italic>of strong</italic> (ref. to Cant. V, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>marble</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Cant. R. to V, 11; Yalk. ib. 991, v. עֶשֶׁת.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<language-key> ch. </language-key>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> Targ. O. Deut. XXXII, 24. Targ. Ex. XXI, 24. Targ. I Kings X, 22 (v. פִּילָא I). Ib. 18. Targ. I Sam. XIV, 4; a. fr.—Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>b</sup> bot; האי שִׁינָּךְ וכ' how is that tooth of thine?; Y. Keth. XII, 35
<sup>a</sup> bot.; Gen. R. s. 33. Ib. יהב ידיה על שִׁינֵּיה וכ' he put his hand on his (Rabbi’s) tooth, and it was cured.—Gitt. 68
<sup>b</sup> ומנח להו אש' דטורא וכ' he puts it (the Shamir) on the peak of a mountain, and the mountain bursts. Snh. 96
<sup>b</sup> תא אש' דטורא (Rashi דטורי) come (to Jerusalem) even if it be necessary to march over the cliffs of mountains (differ. in Rashi); Yalk. Is. 287; a. fr.—ש' דדור, שן דור pr. n. pl. 
<italic>the Cliff of Dor</italic> (v. Hildesh. Beitr. pp. 4; 10). Y. Shebi. VI, 36
<sup>c</sup> (not דרור); Tosef. ib. IV, 11 שורא דרור (corr. acc.); 
<pgbrk id="pg1604" />Sifré Deut. 51 [read:] מדבר שר שן דור; Yalk. ib. 874 (corr. acc.).—
<plural-form>Pl. שִׁנִּין, שִׁנַּיָּא, שִׁנֵּי, שִׁי'</plural-form>. Targ. Am. IV, 6 (not שְׁנִין). Targ. Prov. X, 26.—Targ. Jer. XLIX, 16. Targ. Y. Gen. XLIX, 21 (not שֵׁינֵי); a. fr.—Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>b</sup> תלת … חשש (ב)שִׁינּוֹי suffered from tooth-ache for thirteen years. Ib. חד שִׁינַּיי וכ' one of my teeth annoys me; (Y. Keth. l. c. חד שינא).—Sabb. 82
<sup>a</sup>, v. כַּרְכְּשָׁא; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01559">
<head-word>שָׂנֵא</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to hate</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. 49
<sup>b</sup> גדולה שנאה ששׂוֹנְאִין וכ' great is the hatred with which the ignorant hate the scholar, even greater than that which gentiles bear towards Israel. Ib. 113
<sup>b</sup> שלשה שׂוֹנְאָן three classes of men does the Lord hate. Ib. שלשה שונאין זה וכ' three kinds of creatures hate one another, the dog &c. Ib. מצוה לִשְׂנֹאתוֹ (Var. מותר) it is right (permitted) to hate him. Ib. שִׂנְאוּ את אדניכם hate your masters. Snh. 108
<sup>b</sup> the raven said to Noah, רבך שׂוֹנְאֵנִי ואתה שְׂנֵאתַנִי thy master (God) hates me, and thou hatest me. Ab. I, 10 אהוב … ושְׂנָא וכ' love work and hate office; a. fr.—Part. pass. שָׂנוּא; f. שְׂנוּאָה &c. Kidd. 68
<sup>a</sup>; Yeb. 23
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Deut. XXI, 15) וכי יש ש' לפני המקום וכ' is there before God a hated one and a beloved one (could it be supposed that the law should allow a discrimination between the children of a favored and of a hated wife)? Ib. ש' בנישואיה, v. נִישּׂוּאִין; a. e.—Sifra K’doshim, Par. 3, ch. VIII שָׂנְאוּי.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׂנָא, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׂתַּנֵּא</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be hated</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 4
<sup>8</sup> הר ס̇ינ̇י שבו נִשְׂנְאוּ וכ' it is called Mount Sinai, because on it the gentiles became hateful to the Lord &c. (v. שִׂנְאָה); Yalk. Is. 363 נִשְׂתַּנְּאוּ. Taan. 7
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to ישנא, Koh. VIII, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> א"ת ישונא אלא יִשָּׂנֵא read not 
<italic>y’shunne</italic> (shall be changed), but 
<italic>yissane</italic> (shall be hated).</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses></binyan>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. s. 14 (ref. to Koh. l. c.) יְשׂוּנֶּא יְסוּנֶּה בסמ"ך read 
<italic>y’sunne</italic>, with Samekh (v. supra).</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="U01571">
<head-word>שָׁנָה</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="J00698">ישן</xref>, 
<xref rid="A00083">v. Halévy</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> , Revue des Et.</definition>
<notes> Juives XI, 1885, p. 64) 
<italic>year</italic>. Ber. 55
<sup>a</sup> שלשה … ש' טובה וכ' three things must be prayed for: a good king, a good year, and a good dream. R. Hash. I, 1, a. fr. ראש הש', v. רֹאשׁ. Ib. 2
<sup>a</sup> עלתה לו ש' it is counted as one year of his reign (his second year begins). Y. Yoma V, 42
<sup>c</sup> top; Bab. ib. 53
<sup>b</sup>, v. גָּשַׁם. Ib. 39
<sup>b</sup> אותה ש' … בש' זו הוא מת (on the Day of Atonement of) the year in which Simon the righteous died, he said to them, in this year he (euphem. for I) shall die. Snh. 97
<sup>a</sup>; Ab. Zar. 9
<sup>a</sup> ששת אלפים ש' וכ' the world will last six thousand years. Naz. 5
<sup>a</sup> אותה ש' … שנת עשר וכ' the year in which they asked for a king was the tenth year of office of Samuel &c. Par. I, 1 בת שְׁנָתָהּ in her first year; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שָׁנִים,</plural-form> constr. שְׁנוֹת (שְׁנֵי). Naz. l. c. ימים שאין עמהן ש' ‘days’ in the Scriptures to which the word ‘years’ is not attached; זה שיש עמו ש' this passage (Gen. XLI, </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> where ‘years’ is combined with days. Yoma 71
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Prov. III, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> וכי יש ש' של חיים ויש ש' שאינן וכ' are there years of life, and years of no life? אלו שְׁנוֹתָיו של אדם וכ' those are a man’s years which are changed for him from evil to good.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 89
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to כשנים, Is. I, 18) אם יהיו חטאיכם כש' הללו וכ' if your sins were as many as the years that have been arranged and have come down from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white &c.; Yalk. Is. 256; Y. Sabb. IX, 12
<sup>a</sup> bot. כש' שבין וכ' as the years (required for travelling) between the heaven and the earth; כשְׁנֵי אבות as the years of the patriarchs; a. v. fr.—ברכת הש' (the blessing of the harvests of the year)

<entry id="U01585">
<head-word>שני</head-word>
<head-word>שָׁנָה</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to repeat, do a second time</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yoma 86
<sup>b</sup> ואם ש' בהן וכ' but if he committed the same sins again, he must confess them. Ib. כיון … וש' בה וכ' when a man commits a sin and repeats it, it appears to him permitted; M. Kat. 27
<sup>b</sup>. Ib. 16
<sup>b</sup>; Ber. 18
<sup>a</sup> אם קרית לא שָׁנִיתָ ואם שנית וכ' if thou hast read (studied), thou hast not repeated, and if thou hast repeated, thou hast not reviewed a third time, and if thou hast done so, they have not explained it to thee (v. פָּרַשׁ). Sot. 9
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to Mal. III, 6) לא … ושָׁנִיתִי לה וכ' I never struck a nation and had to do it a second time, but you, children of Israel, have not been consumed; Yalk. Deut. 825. Ib. שהיה מכה … ולא שֹׁונֶה לו who used to strike a man once and no more (killed with one stroke). Tosef. Toh. IV, 1 אומר לו שיִשְׁנֶה we say to him that he should do it again (when it will be seen whether it can be done without touching uncleanness); אין שֹׁונִין בטהרות we must not try again for the purpose of deciding in matters of levitical cleanness; Nidd. 5
<sup>b</sup> אומרים לו שְׁנֵה ושונה we say to him, do it again, and he does it again; a. fr.—Part. pass. שָׁנוּי; f. שְׁנוּיָה &c. Meg. 31
<sup>a</sup>; Ab. Zar. 19
<sup>b</sup>, v. שָׁלַשׁ; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (denom. of מִשְׁנָה) 
<italic>to study the Mishnah</italic>; in gen. 
<italic>to study; to teach</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Meg. 28
<sup>b</sup>; Nidd. 73
<sup>a</sup> כל השונה וכ' he who studies (reviews) traditional laws every day. Meg. 32
<sup>a</sup>; Treat. Sof’rim III, 10 השונה בלא זמרה who studies (Mishnah and Gemarah) without chant. B. Mets. 44
<sup>a</sup> שנית לנו … ותִשְׁנֶה לנו וכ' in thy earlier days thou taughtest us …, and again in thy old days, thou teachest us &c.?; Ab. Zar. 52
<sup>b</sup>. Erub. 92
<sup>a</sup> וכי רבי לא שְׁנָאָהּ וכ' but if Rabbi has not taught that, whence could R. Ḥiyya have it?; Yeb. 43
<sup>a</sup>; Nidd. 62
<sup>a</sup> רבי לא שנה וכ' Rabbi has not taught this? whence &c.? Yeb. 108
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. מי שש' זו לא ש' זו he who taught this, has not taught that, i.e. the two clauses in the Mishnah are from different authors, v. תַּבְרָא. Ḥull. 85
<sup>a</sup> ראה רבי … ושְׁנָאָן וכ' Ms. M. (ed. ושנאו) Rabbi approved of the opinion of R. …, and embodied it in the Mishnah as the opinion of ‘the scholars’. Pes. 3
<sup>b</sup>; Ḥull. 63
<sup>b</sup> לעולם יִשְׁנֶה אדם לתלמידו וכ' one should always teach his pupil the shortest way (use the briefest terms). Ib. 81
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. לא שָׁנוּ אלא וכ' they have taught this only with regard to a case &c., i.e. this is meant only when &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab. Nidd. 22
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. במחלוקת שנויה, v. מַחֲלֹוקֶת.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׁנֶה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be repeated</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Snh. 59
<sup>a</sup> ונִישְׁנֵית, v. נֹחַ. Ḥull. 63
<sup>b</sup> למה נִשְׁנוּ בבהמה וכ' why are the laws of clean and unclean animals repeated (in Deut.)? With reference to quadrupeds, on account of 
<italic>hassh’suʿah</italic> (Deut. XIV, 7, which is not found in Lev. XI, 4) &c., v. שְׁסוּעָה; Bekh. 6
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be taught</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Mets. 33
<sup>b</sup>; B. Kam. 94
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. בימי רבי נשנית משנה זו this Mishnah was taught (originated) in Rabbi’s days. Ber. 28
<sup>a</sup>, v. עֵדוּת; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִשְׁנֶה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to teach</italic> (Mishnah &c.).</definition>
<notes> Lam. R. to I, 6 הַשְׁנֵינִי פרק וכ', v. קָרָא II; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שִׁנָּה, שִׁינָּה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to repeat, to come a second time</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Snh. III, 21
<sup>b</sup> bot. לְשַׁנֹּות, v. טַעֲנָה. Num. R. s. 4
<sup>20</sup> ולא שִׁינְּתָה, v. שָׁלַשׁ.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to change, vary, modify; to make a distinction</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Mets. VI, 2 כל המְשַׁנֶּה ידיו וכ', v. יָד. Snh. 92
<sup>b</sup> אפי' … לא יְשַׁנֶּה אדם את עצמו וכ' even in time of danger (persecution) a man must not change himself from (disguise the insignia of) his office. Yeb. 65
<sup>b</sup> מותר … לשנות וכ' one may modify (the report of a person’s utterances) in the interest of peace. Ib. גדול … הקב"ה ש' בו וכ' peace is a great thing, for even the Lord modified (Sarah’s words) for its sake (ref. to Gen. XVIII, 12 a. 13). Y. Pes. IV, 30
<sup>d</sup> top אל תְּשַׁנּוּ מנהג וכ' change not the usage of your fathers &s. Gen. R. s. 48 זה אחד … שׁשִׁינּוּ וכ' this is one of the things which they (the seventy translators) changed for king Ptolemee. Sabb. 10
<sup>b</sup> לעולם אל יְשַׁנֶּה אדם בנו בין הבנים a man must never distinguish his son among his sons (favor one son more than the others); Gen. R. s. 84. Bets. 30
<sup>a</sup> אם אי אפשר לשנות if it is not possible to do the thing in a different manner (so as to be reminded that it is a Holy Day). Tanḥ. Nitsabim 3 כבר … שלא אֲשׁנֶּה בכם וכ' I have sworn to you that I will not change my relation to you &c. Yalk. Mal. 589 מי שי' במי which of us changed his conduct towards the other?; המקום לא שי' בישראל God has not changed his relation to Israel; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְשׁוּנֶּה; f. מְשׁוּנָּה. Y. Taan. I, end, 64
<sup>d</sup> עורב יצא מש' מן הבריות the raven came out of the ark looking different from all other creatures (black). Shek. V, 2, v. רִצְפָה. Sabb. 56
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to II Sam. XII, 9) מש' רעה זו וכ' this evil deed is different from all &c. Ib. 156
<sup>b</sup> מיתה מש' a strange (unnatural, sudden) death; Sot. 35
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—Deut. R. s. 9 ראה אותו מש' he saw him (the angel of death) looking strange (excited); מפני מה אתה מש' why art thou excited?</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִשְׁתַּנֶּה, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׁתַּנֶּה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be changed, different</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Snh. 38
<sup>a</sup> בשלשה … מִשְׁתַּנֶּה מחבירו וכ' by three things one man is distinguishable from another: by his voice &c. Pes. X, 4 (116
<sup>a</sup>) מה נ' הלילה וכ' why is this night different 
<pgbrk id="pg1606" />from all other nights? Snh. 71
<sup>b</sup> [read:] הואיל ונ' דינו ונִשְׁתַּנֵית מיתתו because his (the proselyte’s) legal status is different, and the mode of capital punishment is different for him. Sabb. 53
<sup>b</sup> נִשְׁתַּנּוּ לו סדרי וכ' the order of nature had to be changed for him. R. Hash. 19
<sup>a</sup> מה נִישְׁתַּנִּינוּ מכל וכ' wherein are we different from any other nation or tongue that you decree for us such hard decrees?; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="U01586">
<head-word>שְׁנֵי</head-word>
<head-word>שְׁנָא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to repeat</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. I Sam. XXVI, 8 ed. Wil. (v. תְּנֵי).—Snh. 59
<sup>a</sup> ולמה לי למִישְׁנֵי בסיני and why is it repeated at Sinai?; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to change; to be different</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. O. Deut. XXXIV, 7.—Lev. R. s. 22 כל מאי דהוה הדין ש' הדין ש' as the one (the mosquito) changed, so did the other (Titus) change. Yeb. 21
<sup>b</sup> או דילמא לא שנא (abbrev. ל"ש) or is there no difference (between the wife of a brother on the mother’s side and that of a brother on the father’s side)? Succ. 29
<sup>b</sup> ל"ש ביו"ט … ול"ש וכ' no difference whether it is the first Holy Day or the second. Ib. 30
<sup>a</sup> ל"ש לפני וכ' no difference whether before &c. Sabb. 6
<sup>a</sup> הכי נמי ל"ש in this case, too, it is the same; a. v. fr.—Yeb. l. c. מאי ש' הני מאי ש' הא (abbrev. מ"ש) what difference is there between the former and the latter? Sabb. 4
<sup>a</sup> ומאי ש' and wherein lies the difference? Ib. 2
<sup>b</sup> מ"ש הכא … ומ"ש התם וכ' wherein lies the difference (what reason is there) that the Mishnah says here, ‘two which are four within, and two which are four without’, and there (Shebu. I, 1) only, ‘two which are four’?; a. fr.—
<italic>Part</italic>. שָׁאנֵי 
<italic>it is different</italic>. Succ. 21
<sup>b</sup> ש' שוורים הואיל וכ' it is different in the case of oxen, because &c. Sabb. 7
<sup>b</sup> ש' צרור וכ' it is different with bundles and other objects &c. Ker. 11
<sup>a</sup> והכא ש' but here it is different; a. v. fr.—V. שׁנִיא.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שַׁנֵּי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to change; to act strangely</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XLI, 14. Targ. Ps. LXXXIX, 35. Ib. XXXIV, 1. Targ. Y. II Deut. XXXII, 5; a. fr.—[Ib. 41 אישני, read: אישנן, v. שְׁנַן.—Targ. Jud. XX, 16 משנן, read: משגן, v. שְׁגֵי.]—Taan. 24
<sup>b</sup> שַׁנִּי דוכתיך change thy place; ש' דוכתיה he changed his place. Ker. 11
<sup>a</sup> לישנא דשׁנּוּיֵי, v. חָרַף. Bets. 30
<sup>a</sup> כמה דאפשר לשנויי מְשַׁנִּינָן וכ' as much as it is feasible to change (the mode of doing a thing), we must change on the Holy Day; Sabb. 128
<sup>b</sup>; ib. 117
<sup>b</sup> מְשַׁנִּין. Bets. l. c. והא הני נשי … ולא מְשַׁנְּיָין וכ' but there are those women that fill their pitchers … without any change, and we say nothing to them (to interfere)! Snh. 96
<sup>a</sup> top שני נפשך (Rashi אַשְׁנִי) disguise thyself; במאי אִישַׁנֵּי how shall I disguise (myself)?; Yalk. Is. 276; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to reply</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 7
<sup>b</sup> זימנין מְשַׁנֵּי לה וכ' at times he replied to it (met the objection by saying) &c. Ib. 3
<sup>b</sup> דמשני לך; Keth. 98
<sup>b</sup> דשַׁנִּינָן, v. שִׁינּוּיָא. Pes. 20
<sup>b</sup> ומְשַׁנֵּי שאני התם וכ' and he answered, it is different in that case; a. fr.—Shebu. 21
<sup>a</sup> top כדשני ליה (Rashi כדמשני) as he (Abayi) replied to him (R. Papa, further below).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַשְׁנֵי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to change, act strangely</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Mal. III, 6. Targ. O. a. Y. I Deut. XXXII, 5; a. fr.—[Targ. Ps. LXXI, 17 אשני, read with ed. Lag. אתני.]—Snh. 96
<sup>a</sup> top, v. supra.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִשְׁתַּנֵּי, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִשְׁתְּנֵי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be changed</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Deut. l. c. Targ. Lam. IV, 1; a. e.—Snh. 71
<sup>b</sup> נימא הואיל וא' א' let us say, because his status has changed, he is a different person (not responsible for acts committed in his previous condition); האי דינו א' מיתתו לא א' this man’s legal status has changed, but the mode of his execution is not affected thereby. <sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>second</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Meg. IV, 1 בש' on the second day of the week. Ib. 22
<sup>a</sup>; Taan. 27
<sup>b</sup> הש' קורא וכ' the second (of those called to read from the Law) reads &c. Bets. 6
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. יום טוב ש' the second (Rabbinical) Holy Day (instituted on account of the uncertainty of the calendar). Sabb. 40
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. כלי ש' second vessel, i.e. a vessel into which a boiling mass has been poured, contrad. to כלי ראשון a vessel direct from the fire.—Maas. Sh. I, 1, a. fr. מעשר ש', v. מַעֲשֵׂר.—Esp. 
<italic>a</italic>) (לטומאה) ש' 
<italic>the second degree of levitical uncleanness, an object made unclean through contact with uncleanness</italic>, v. רִאשׁוֹן. Toh. II, 2 האוכל … אוכל ש' ש' he that eats food unclean in the second degree, becomes unclean in the second degree. Pes. 14
<sup>a</sup> ש' וש' הוא וכ' it is a contact between two things both unclean in the second degree, and why do you say that he adds to the degree of uncleanness?; a. fr.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>relationship in the second degree, second generation</italic>. Snh. 28
<sup>a</sup> ש' בש' תנן we have learned that a relative in the second degree (first cousin) cannot testify for or against a relative in the second degree; ש' בראשון תנן we have learned that one of the second generation cannot testify for or against one of the first generation, i.e. his uncle. Ib. שלישי בש' a relative in the third degree against one in the second degree, i.e. his father’s first cousin; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׁנִיִּים</plural-form>. Yad. II, 2 ואת הש' למקום אחר and water poured over his hands a second time on another place. Ib. ועל הש' טהור and a loaf which fell on the place which received the second water is clean. Gen. R. s. 31 ש' לו וכ' the second story of the ark was for him (Noah) and his sons and the clean animals; a. fr.—
<italic>Fem</italic>. שְׁנִיָּה, שְׁנִיָּיה. Shek. III, 4; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׁנִיּוֹת</plural-form>. Yad. III, 2 ש' (sub. לטומאה), v. supra. Ab. Zar. 3
<sup>b</sup> ש' during the second three hours of the day; a. fr.—Esp. שניה (sub. לערוה) 
<italic>incest of second degree, intermarriage forbidden by rabbinical enactment</italic>. Yeb. 21
<sup>b</sup> אמו ערוה אם אמו ש' connection with one’s mother is incest, with one’s mother’s mother incest in the second degree. Ib. משום ש' as incest of the second degree; a. fr.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as above. Ib.
<sup>a</sup> מה הם ש' what relationships are 
<italic>sh’niyoth?</italic> Ib. (ref. to Lev. XVIII, 27) האל … מאי נינהו ש' 
<italic>haël</italic> means the severe, which implies that there are milder forms of incest; what are they? The 
<italic>sh’niyoth</italic>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01628">
<head-word>שִׁעְבֵּד</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Shafel of עָבַד) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to subject, subjugate, surrender; to obligate, pledge</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 44 (ref. to Gen. XV, 13) ידוע שאני מְשׁעְבְּדָן וכ' ‘knowing’ means that I will surrender them as slaves, ‘thou shalt know’, that I will redeem them. Pesik. R. s. 15 לא כך … שהוא מְשַׁעְבְּדֵינוּ בשבעים וכ' has not the Lord said, that he will make us the subjects of seventy nations? Ib. [read:] גותי אחד בא ומְשַׁעְבֵּד באחד ממנו כגון שׁשִׁיעְבְּדָה כל אומתו one Goth comes and enslaves one of us, that is as much as if she (Rome) had enslaved all of us; Cant. R. to II, 8. Gen. R. s. 85 (ref. to Is. LXVI, 7) קודם … מְשַׁעְבֵּד ראשון וכ' before yet the first oppressor (of Israel) was born, the last redeemer was born. R. Hash. III, 8 (ref. to Num. XXI, 8) בזמן … ומְשַׁעְבְּדִין את לבם לאביהם וכ' when the Israelites looked upward and pledged their hearts to their Father in heaven, they were healed; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְשׁוּעְבָּד; 
<plural-form>pl. מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים, מְשׁוּעְבָּדִין</plural-form>. Num. R. s. 5
<sup>8</sup> שלא … אלא מש' לפני הארון they were not haughty, but bore themselves like servants before the Ark. Y. Hag. III, 79
<sup>b</sup> שיהא הכל מש' להלכה so that everything be made subject to the law; a. e.—נכסים מש', or משועבדין (sub. נכסים) 
<italic>mortgaged property</italic>, i.e. property bought from a person who owes a debt collectible from his landed estate in whatever hands it may be, opp. בני חורין property in the hands of the debtor. B. Mets. 13
<sup>b</sup>. Gitt. 50
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to vex, persecute, attempt to destroy</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ex. R. s. 22 נראה … מְשַׁעְבְּדִין את ישראל בדבר וכ' (not על ישראל) let us see how we can persecute Israel by means of something which the Lord cannot bring upon us in the same manner; Yalk. ib. 208 אם מְשַׁעְבְּדִים אנו אותם באש וכ' if we destroy them through fire, their God can bring fire upon us &c.; בואו ונְשַׁעְבְּדֵם במים (not ונשתעבדם) come, let us destroy them through water; Yalk. Ps. 786; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (with (with ל) 
<italic>to be subjugated, be the slave</italic> or 
<italic>subject of</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gitt. IV, 4 עבד … אם לשום עבד יִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד וכ' a slave that was captured and redeemed, if he was redeemed as a slave, remains a slave; if as a freeman, he cannot be made a slave. Ib. 37
<sup>b</sup> ישתעבד לרבו ראשון he is the slave of his first (original) master; לא ישתעבד … לרבו שני he is the slave neither of his first master, nor of his second master (his redeemer). Pesik. R. s. 15 במה … או שׁיִשְׁתַּעְבְּדו למלכיות which wilt thou choose? that thy children go down to Gehenna, or that they be subjected to successive empires? Sabb. 88
<sup>b</sup> אמר … לפרעה הִשְׁתַּעְבַּדְתֶּם (Ms. M. נִשְׁתַּעְבַּדְתֶּם) he (Moses) said to them (the angels), did you go down to Egypt? 
<pgbrk id="pg1609" />have you been slaves to Pharaoh? Midr. Till. to Ps. LXXVIII, 32 (insert from Yalk. ib. 819) זה יעקב … שאילו עלה לא ירד עוד ולא היה לנו להִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד שיעבוד זה שאנו משועבדין (v. ed. Bub.) this refers to Jacob …, for if he had gone up, he would not have gone down again, and we should not have to suffer the servitude to which we are now subjected; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (with ב) 
<italic>to use as slave, enslave</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. 118
<sup>b</sup> מה הללו שנִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ בהן כך אני שלא נִשְׁתַּעְבַּדְתִּי וכ' if they (the Egyptians) who treated them as slaves, fare thus, I (Cush) who did not enslave them &c. Gitt. 40
<sup>a</sup> פלונית … אל ישתעבדו בה וכ' that handmaid of mine, they (my heirs) shall not treat her as a slave after my death. Keth. 111
<sup>a</sup> השביע … שלא ישתעבדו בהן וכ' the Lord adjured the nations not to oppress Israel too hard. Men. 53
<sup>b</sup>; Yalk. Jer. 289 [read:] ישתעבדו בהם ארבע מלכיות וכ' (v. Rabb. D. S. to Men. l. c., note) four successive empires shall treat them as slaves, each as long &c.; a. fr.—[Yalk. Ex. 208, v. supra.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sense>

<sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to apportion, estimate, measure, calculate</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. VII, 4 כיצד מְשׁעֲרִין אותה וכ' how do we define the proportions of the mixture (to find out whether the forbidden admixture is large enough to impart its taste to the permitted portion)? As if it were an admixture of meat in a vegetable dish. Ib. 97
<sup>b</sup> כשהן משערין משערין וכ' when we define the proportions, we include in the calculation the broth &c. Ib. כל איסורין … מְשַׁעֲרִינָן וכ' in all admixtures of Biblically forbidden matter we assume for calculation that the forbidden matter was onions or porret. Ib. שִׁיעֲרוּ חכמים וכ' the scholars have calculated that of all forbidden substances none give a stronger taste than onions &c. Lev. R. s. 37 מְשָׁעֵר את … באיטלקית (some ed. מְשָׁעֵיר) do you estimate that in all I drank at my meal there would have been a quarter of a Log of Italian (unmixed) wine? Koh. R. to V, 8 שיערו אותה, v. next w.; a. fr.—Midr. Till. to Ps. CXIV (expl. סֹלּוּ, Ps. LXVIII, 5) שַׁעֲרוּ לפניו דרכיכם (not שיע'; ed. Bub. שפרו, a glossator’s emendation) measure your ways before the Lord (cmp. שׁוּם I). Pesik. Zutr. Haaz. (ed. Bub. p. 114) (ref. to שערום, Deut. XXXII, 17) לא שִׁיעֲרוּם וכ' whom your fathers never appraised, to find out whether or not they are of use; Yalk. Deut. 545 לא שערום.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="U01681">שַׁעַר</xref>) 
<italic>to superintend the market</italic>, v. מְשָׁעֵר.</definition>

<sup>a</sup> האומר לשִׁפְחָתוֹ וכ' if one says to his bondwoman, be thou free, but thy child (with which thou goest) shall be a slave, the child follows her status (is free). Ib. ש' כנענית a Canaanite slave. Keth. V, 5 הכניסה לו ש' אחת וכ' if the wife brought him one slave, she need not grind, or bake &c.; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. שְׁפָחוֹת</plural-form>. Ib. אפי' … מאה ש' וכ' even if she brought him a hundred slaves, he may force her (his wife) to work in wool &c. Ker. 9
<sup>a</sup> ש' חרופות, v. חֲרוּפָה. Lev. R. s. 16, a. e. ש' מכודנות, v. כָּדַן. Tanḥ. Vayetsé 8 לא תהא … הש' should not my sister Rachel be at least like one of the handmaids (Bilhah and Zilpah)? Ab. II, 7; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="U01734">

<head-word>שָׁפָה</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="U00488"> cmp. שׁוּף II)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to crush.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—Part. pass</italic>. שָׁפוּי, 
<plural-form>pl. שְׁפוּיִין</plural-form>
<italic>crushed, humble, contrite</italic> (= b. h. דַּכָּא). Tosef. Ḥag. II, 9 עניו וש' humble and contrite; Tosef. Snh. VII, 1 וש' (only); Y. ib. I, 19
<sup>c</sup>. Gen. R. s. 60 דווין וש' Ar. (ed. ושפופין) broken down and crushed (poor); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to rub, smooth, plane.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—Part. pass</italic>. as ab. 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>smooth</italic>. Koh. R. to XII, 14 two paths אחד ש' ואחד מלא וכ' one smooth, and the other full of thorns and pebbles.—Yalk. Gen. 62 בור ש' (Snh. 109
<sup>a</sup> שָׁאפֵי; Ar. שפת, corr. acc.) a smooth (blank, empty) pit, v. בּוֹרְסִיף.—
<italic>b</italic>) (cmp. חָלָק) 
<italic>unimpaired, unscathed</italic>. Gen. R. s. 45, v. רָתַק.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>שִׁפָּה, שִׁי'</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to plane, saw, trim</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. 125
<sup>a</sup> קולית שש' וכ' a thigh-bone which one sawed through lengthwise. Ab. Zar. 42
<sup>a</sup> ישראל שש' ע"ז וכ' if an Israelite chipped off an idol whether for his own purpose (to use the wood) or for its sake (to improve its appearance). Ib. 49
<sup>b</sup>. Y. Gitt. V, 47
<sup>a</sup> bot. גזלו ושִׁיפָּהוּ if he took a block by force and planed it. Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. III, 1 שפת הימנה וכ' (read: שפה) if he filed off a part of it and made of it &c.; 
<pgbrk id="pg1615" />a. e.—Part. pass. מְשׁוּפֶּה; 
<plural-form>pl. מְשׁוּפִּים, מְשׁוּפִּין</plural-form>. Y. Gitt. l. c. גזלו מש' if he took it planed. Y. Succ. I, 52
<sup>c</sup> top במש' לכלים (not בכלים) when the boards are planed preparatory to making them into utensils; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to smooth, polish</italic>, Kel. XIV, 5 משׁיְשַׁפֶּנּוּ Ar.; Ned. 56
<sup>b</sup> משׁיְשַׁפֵּם, v. 
<xref rid="U00490">שׁוּף II</xref>.—Trnsf.</definition>
<notes>
<italic>to pacify, give satisfaction</italic>. Y. B. Mets. V, 10
<sup>b</sup> המבטל … חייב לשַׁפּוֹת לו if a tenant or an agent neglects his neighbor’s field, he must indemnify him; ib. IX, beg. 12
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to leave smooth places</italic>, (cmp. חָלַק 
<italic>Hif.</italic>) 
<italic>to plant wide apart</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Orl. I, beg. 60
<sup>c</sup> לקורות במְשַׁפֶּה (or במַשְׁפֶּה 
<italic>Hif.</italic>) when he plants the trees wide apart, it is an indication that he wants to raise them for beams, opp. רָצַף. B. Bath. V, 4 הגדילו לא יְשַׁפֶּה (or יַשְׁפֶּה) if they (the trees bought in a person’s field) grew large, he (the owner of the field) has no right to smooth the field (cut the trees down). Ib. הגדילו ישפה when they are grown large, he (the owner of the trees) may cut them (in order to use the ground they occupy); a. e.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<italic>Pe.</italic>; h. text דכית). Ib. LXXXIX, 11; a. e.</notes></sense>

<number>—2)</number>
